channel.title: OctoProbe News
channel.description: OctoProbe News is an investigative desk published by Redwing Technologies LLC. The feed carries its reporting on national security, intelligence, digital targeting, influence operations, and news verification through public records.

item.title: Handala’s Livni Phone “Leak” and the Signature Reduction Requirements of War
item.description: Handala, an Iran-linked persona, leaked Tzipi Livni’s texts and contacts. What the hack proved, what was psyop, and what officials must cut from their signature.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: OctoProbe cover over a dark street map of Tel Aviv with a red pin: a cutout portrait of former Israeli Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni beside the headline The Livni Phone “Leak,” Signature Reduction in War.

item.title: ‘$50 Million Per Day’: Feds Say the Miami Broker Behind ‘TheAlienEx’ Worked for a Russian Laundering Network
item.description: A DEA affidavit ties Miami broker Pavel Kulizhnikov to @TheAlienEx_manager and the JUST Team, a network a source estimated launders $50 million a day.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover art with the headline A $50 Million-a-Day Laundering Claim over a dark map of the Miami and Fort Lauderdale coast, with the orange alien-mascot logo of TheAlienEx linked by an orange line to an abstract identifier graph, and, on the right, an orange-framed TheAlienEx promotional image of an alien mascot in a car holding cash under the Russian slogan ОБМЕН ВАЛЮТ ПО-МАЙАМСКИ (Currency exchange, Miami-style).

item.title: From $10 Million Bounty to the Oval Office: The Record Behind Julani’s Rebrand
item.description: How Abu Muhammad al-Julani rebranded as Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa: U.S. designation and delisting records, DIA files on American TOW missiles in Syria, a geolocation of his Idlib appearances, and the human rights record of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover art showing a cutout of Abu Muhammad al-Julani in a white turban and camouflage jacket on the right, over a dark map of northwestern Syria with Idlib Governorate outlined in red, under the headline From Terrorist to Politician.

item.title: SOCOM Promised ‘Close Coordination’ for Its Online Psyops Hub. Pentagon Watchdogs Found the Gaps.
item.description: FOIA records and inspector general reports on SOCOM’s Joint MISO WebOps Center, CENTCOM’s earlier web operations, military deception planning, and the line between influence work and intelligence collection.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover art with the title page of DoD Inspector General report DODIG-2024-085, Evaluation of Combatant Command Joint Military Deception Planning, over a dark map of Tampa with a pin on the planned MISO facility site at MacDill Air Force Base, under the headline Inside the Pentagon’s Online Psyops Hub.

item.title: Inside Samolet, the Russian Homebuilder the EU Says Used North Korean Workers
item.description: OSINT on Samolet Group under EU North Korea sanctions: the Official Journal entries, Samolet’s network, the Vladivostok site in city video, its sitemap, CEO Anna Akinshina, and the filings after October 12, 2026.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover: the Samolet entry from the EU Official Journal annex, listing “Samolet Group of Companies” PJSC with its Moscow address, OGRN 1187746590283, INN 9731004688, associated individual Anna Nikolaevna Akinshina, designation date 12.10.2026, and the EU’s reasons, beside a frame from the Vladivostok city video showing a worker crouched by a water tank at a construction site.

item.title: The White House Cyber Office Blacked Out Its Huawei, TikTok, and Kaspersky Slides. The Laws Behind Them Are Public.
item.description: Two Office of the National Cyber Director FOIA releases withhold its Huawei, TikTok, and Kaspersky slides under (b)(5). Here are the public authorities behind them, NSPM-13, and Biden’s counterterrorism memo, NSM-13.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Dark street map of Washington with the Office of the National Cyber Director seal and a slide titled Ex 1, Huawei and 5G Radio Access Network Kits, its body covered by a (b)(5) redaction box, beside the words What the Cyber Office Kept Back.

item.title: An Iraqi Bank Sponsored Baghdad’s Anti-Money-Laundering Conference. Treasury Says It Sent Iran Dollars Every Month.
item.description: Iraq’s International Development Bank sponsored a Baghdad AML conference, then OFAC sanctioned it on October 15, 2026 for sending Iran dollars.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Dark street map of Baghdad’s Karrada district with a red map pin and an illustration of a generic stone-and-glass bank building with columns, beside the words Dollars for Tehran, via Baghdad.

item.title: The Tech-Support Scam Infoblox Exposed Is Still Running, From a Server Not on Its List
item.description: Help TDS, the tech-support scam Infoblox tied to operator Hotejka, was still running from a new Frankfurt server behind a shared decoy page.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Dark street map of Frankfurt with a red map pin and an abstract white node-and-line graph, beside the words The Scam Server That Moved.

item.title: Panama Law Firm Was Tied to Iran’s Shadow Fleet Three Years Before Treasury Sanctioned It
item.description: Karnakis and Karnakis, sanctioned October 21, 2026: the earliest public report, the seven companies sanctioned first, and how openly the firm operated.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cutouts of five Karnakis and Karnakis staff photos from the firm’s website, outlined in red and overlapping at lower right, on a dark street map of Panama City, beside the words The Law Firm Behind the Fleet.

item.title: Treasury Sanctioned Whales Shipping Line. Its Company Profile Still Names Its Staff.
item.description: OFAC sanctioned Dubai ship agent Whales Shipping Line on October 21, 2026. Its company profile, website, and two blocked boats, traced through public records.

media:content.media:description: Dark OctoProbe map cover of the Indian Ocean with markers for ships sanctioned on October 21, 2026, titled Tracking Iran’s Shadow Fleet.

item.title: Pegasus Took a Phone’s Past. AI Makes It Attributable
item.description: Op-ed: NSO’s own Pegasus 3.0 product description, filed in the WhatsApp case, pitches pulling a phone’s full history. AI makes that past the key to attribution.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Op-ed cover: dark OctoProbe cover over a world map with a drawn smartphone whose screen shows a timeline of message, Wi-Fi, and call records, with fading record bars rising out of the phone, beside the headline Pegasus Took a Phone’s Past

item.title: Signal Encryption Stops at the Endpoint
item.description: sigtop unlocks Signal Desktop’s local store. E2EE is not endpoint security. Messages, media, group membership and UUIDv4 ACIs are the collection surface.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Light OctoProbe cover over a grey North America map on a white field with the blue Signal logo at right and a Signal-blue accent rule beside the black headline Signal Encryption Stops at the Endpoint

media:content.media:description: Dark OctoProbe cover over a map of Stuttgart, Germany, with a red pin on the city and the blue U.S. Army Europe and Africa shield with a flaming sword at right, beside the headline Redacted, Not Useless

item.title: Whose Coffee? An Anti-Bot Developer’s Handle Turns Up on Archive.today’s Donate Link
